incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH GPU QUEUE GROWTH — autoscaler not reacting, queue > 120 for the last 5m. Severity: P1. Alert: GPUQueueHigh (>100), HPAScaleFail metric: adapter_errors=45

sam (oncall-sre): I’m paged, investigating. Noted high qps to /v1/generate and backlog in the inference queue. Pinging @jia @marc.

jia (eng-runtime): seen it on graphs. HPA target (gpu-inference-hpa) showing 0 metrics for CPU/Custom. Prometheus shows adapter scrape backlog.

marc (eng-ml): I’m here. Quick check: are we hitting the cluster GPU quota or node autoscaler limits?

sam (oncall-sre): kubectl get nodes | grep gpu shows all GPU nodepools at capacity. Node autoscaler reported 'scale-up disabled due to resource limits' in CA logs. Also HPA not getting metrics so it's not scaling.

ops-bot: Attached logs from metrics-adapter pod: 
```
E0316 12:37:40.123456 1 adapter.go:212] failed to get metrics from Prometheus: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = context deadline exceeded
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
```

jia (eng-runtime): that panic is concerning — metrics-adapter is crashing and dropping metrics. Prometheus shows a scrape backlog and remote_write queue growing. If adapter is down, HPA won't get custom metrics -> no scale.

sam (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations: 1) Manual horizontal scale of inference replicas to relieve queue; 2) Restart metrics-adapter + metrics-server; 3) If CA blocked, temporarily increase nodepool quota or fall back to dedicated pool. I’ll run manual scale and restart adapter.

sam (oncall-sre): Executing: 
```
kubectl scale deploy/gpu-inference --replicas=12 -n inference
kubectl rollout restart deploy/metrics-adapter -n kube-system
kubectl rollout restart deploy/metrics-server -n kube-system
```

marc (eng-ml): Manual scale accepted. Doing a quick health check on model variants — enabling a smaller quantized variant for low-tier traffic to lower GPU memory and increase throughput.

rachel (customer-success): Noted. I’m drafting a status message for impacted customers (some are seeing timeouts or throttled requests). ETA for an update in 10m.

jia (eng-runtime): After restart, metrics-adapter logs show it reconnecting but reporting dropped series count high. Prometheus scrape backlog is decreasing slowly. HPA still shows no custom metrics; probably need a full adapter pod recycle + check RBAC.

ops-bot: CA (cluster-autoscaler) logs: 
```
I0316 12:41:05.789 CA] ScaleUp: would scale to 5 nodes, but quotaExceeded: cannot increase, project quota would be exceeded
```

sam (oncall-sre): Quota is the blocker for adding nodes. I’m opening infra ticket to request temporary quota bump with cloud team. Meanwhile, we need to preserve SLOs: toggle throttling for free-tier customers and route enterprise customers to Dedicated capacity.

marc (eng-ml): How quickly can we route traffic to Dedicated? We have routing policy but need to flip for some API keys. I can push a config change to the routing service that sends enterprise tenant IDs to dedicated pools.

sam (oncall-sre): Do it. I’ll apply throttling rules: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: throttling-rules
  namespace: inference
data:
  low_tier_qps: "0.5"
  mid_tier_qps: "2"
EOF
```

marc (eng-ml): Routing pushed. Verified about ~30% of traffic moved to dedicated pool. Queue dropped ~25% in next 90s.

jia (eng-runtime): metrics-adapter stable after second restart, but Prometheus remote_write backlog still has ~1.2M samples queued — adapter returning partial metrics. HPA depends on fresh metrics; we can temporarily force HPA to scale using kubectl patch on targetReplicas.

sam (oncall-sre): Manual HPA patch: 
```
kubectl patch hpa gpu-inference-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}' -n inference
```
Applied — replicas now 12. Queue down to 50. Latency improving.

rachel (customer-success): Status update posted: "We are aware of increased latencies/failed requests for inference API. Mitigations in progress, no data loss. Enterprise customers routed to dedicated capacity. Next update in 20m." Customers acknowledging.

jia (eng-runtime): Follow-up: metrics-server crash stack shows root cause was a memory leak in v0.3.4 adapter image. We should pin to v0.3.3 for now. Opening PR to revert image and add liveness probe adjustments.

marc (eng-ml): Also noting that one big job from customer X was consuming many KV cache entries causing increased memory per replica. We evicted the job and asked customer X to retry with smaller batch size.

sam (oncall-sre): Infra quota request approved (temp bump +1 GPU node). CA now allowed to scale. New GPU node provisioned; nodepool size +1. HPA can now scale normally once metrics flow resumes.

ops-bot: Prometheus remote_write queue drained to 200k after provisioning new node; adapter reports metrics back to API server. HPA target metrics now visible: custom/inference_queue_length = 18 -> triggers no further scale.

tina (oncall-next): picking up handoff. Summary for next-oncall: 
- Incident: GPU queue growth caused by metrics-adapter crash & cluster quota blocking CA.
- Actions taken: manual scaling to 12 replicas, restarted metrics-adapter & metrics-server, routed enterprise to Dedicated, applied throttling ConfigMap for low-tier, evicted large customer job, requested temp quota bump and provisioned node.
- Current state: queue ~12-18, replicas 12, adapter stable, Prom remote_write draining.
- Customer impact: increased latency and some timeouts for low-tier customers for ~45m window. Enterprise customers minimally affected after routing.
- Open action items: revert metrics-adapter to v0.3.3 (PR #487), add liveness/readiness tolerations, add runbook step to detect adapter panic earlier, review auto-scaling quotas and CA config, follow up with customer X re: job sizing.

sam (oncall-sre): Handoff accepted. I’ll add detailed timestamps & logs to the incident doc and link runbook.

rachel (customer-success): I’ll follow up with the 3 customers who reported errors and share mitigation details.

marc (eng-ml): Postmortem note: consider autoscale fallback: if HPA metrics missing, enable predictive scaling based on request rate (gateway-level) as a guardrail.

sam (oncall-sre): Incident Resolved: GPUs healthy, HPA metrics restored, queue drained to normal. Will mark P1->P2 in 2h if stable. Creating follow-up task list in #postmortems.

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 2026-03-16T12:53:30Z. Duration: ~46m.
